note: All three are the same unhighlighted single-color vertical bar chart in Sun/Thur/Fri/Sat order with value labels and a 'Fri averages 1.11x Sat' subtitle; attempt 3 differs only in its thin, misaligned bars and a shorter axis label.
All three are the same daily line chart with the same title and layout; attempts 1 and 2 have no callouts, while attempt 3 adds a peak callout and a dashed daily-average line with a legend.

All three are the same rocket-colormap seaborn heatmap of raw counts with no callouts. Only the subtitle wording changes: attempt 1 adds correct/misclassified counts, attempt 2 explains the diagonal and attempt 3 names class_2's lowest recall. Design differences are cosmetic: bold annotations and horizontal y-tick labels in attempt 3.

All three are the same dumbbell chart with the same ordering, colors, legend and value labels; only the subtitle changes, from GB/Germany growth multiples (attempt 1) to the USA's 36.3× jump (attempt 2) to the USA's percentage rise, where the text is garbled by mathtext (attempt 3).

All three use the same red/blue ECDF with a lower-right legend. The annotations differ: attempt 1 has a floating callout arrow that points at nothing, attempt 2 puts the takeaway in a subtitle with no callout, and attempt 3 adds a callout giving the median values.

All three are absolute stacked area charts, but they stack the series in different orders and use different colors. Attempt 1 puts renewables at the bottom; 2 and 3 put fossil fuels at the bottom. The subtitles say different things: attempt 1 gives percent shares, 2 gives percentage points and 3 gives a 15× multiplier. Only attempt 3 adds in-chart callouts, which overlap the data, along with vertical gridlines.

Attempt 1 is a horizontal ridgeline with a gradient fill and a qualitative subtitle. Attempts 2 and 3 are nearly identical violin-plus-jitter charts with red IQR bars, and their subtitles compare a summer month with a winter month using slightly different numbers. None of the three has callouts.

Attempt 1 is a slope chart labeled with values at both ends, attempt 2 is a slope chart labeled with names on the left only and a clipped y-axis, and attempt 3 is a horizontal dumbbell chart; each subtitle draws a different takeaway (Africa and Asia gained the most, Africa gained the least, Asia gained the most).
All three are line charts with the same layout and direct end-of-line labels, differing only in color assignment and label wording; attempt1 is the only one that adds a subtitle takeaway.

All three are the same horizontal bar chart with First class highlighted in dark, bold value labels, and a subtitle saying first class had 2.6x the survival rate of third class; the only differences are the subtitle wording and attempt 1 putting First at the bottom instead of the top.

All three are the same single-color bar chart in cylinder order with bold value labels and an 8-vs-4 '2.0x' subtitle; they differ only in the subtitle wording (attempt 2) and the x-axis label text (attempt 3).

All three use the same diverging red/blue bar chart with a dark rolling-mean line and the same 2024 record callout. They differ only in subtitles: attempt 2 has none, attempt 3 states a quantified takeaway, and attempt 3's legend says 10-year even though its line matches the others' 5-year curve.

All three are the same horizontal grey violin plot with jittered points and red median ticks labeled 5,000/3,700/3,700, and the same Gentoo-vs-Chinstrap 1,300 g subtitle; the only differences are subtitle wording, a 'g' suffix on the attempt 3 labels, and where the jittered points land.

All three are the same min/avg/max dot-range chart in the same order with the same labels; only the title and subtitle wording changes slightly, and every subtitle makes the same two points (ERNIE has the highest average, BiLSTM the widest range).
All three use the same dot-grid probability mesh, contour boundaries, circled misclassified points and identical footnote; only the title wording and the legend placement differ slightly.

All three use the same subtitle about mpg vs weight (r = -0.83), with no callouts and only the titles reworded; attempts 1 and 3 are the same lower-triangle RdBu heatmap, while attempt 2 shows the full 5x5 matrix including the diagonal.

All three use the same 2x2 small-multiples spaghetti plot with a Diet 3 takeaway subtitle. Attempts 1 and 2 add a bold mean line and label the final mean, 1 with leader-line callouts and 2 with 'Final:' boxes against greyed-out individual lines. Attempt 3 has no mean line or callouts, and its subtitle gives different numbers (272g, Diet 1 at 202g).

All three use the same two-panel PR/ROC layout, grey fold curves, a dark average line, an orange dashed no-skill baseline, the same legends and the same AUC-range footnotes; the only change is that attempt 1's title adds the word 'Classifier'.

All three are the same log-scale scatter with the same continent colors, markers and legend placement. Attempts 1 and 2 each add a subtitle saying richer countries live longer, worded differently, while attempt 3 has only a title and no subtitle, and none of them has callouts.

All three use the same multi-line chart with identical colors and direct end labels. Attempt 1 has a stacked, misplaced legend-style label column and a decade-takeaway subtitle, attempt 2 has no subtitle or callouts, and attempt 3 adds a post-2008 recovery takeaway plus a '2008 Crisis' arrow callout.
All three are the same histogram with the same dashed median line labeled 'Median $9.50'; the only difference is that attempt 1's title says 'NYC Taxi Fares' where the others say 'Taxi Fares'.

Attempt 1 is a heatmap with cell values, while attempts 2 and 3 are near-identical grouped bar charts with red/blue sex encoding and percent labels; all three use a title plus a one-line subtitle, but the subtitles make different points (near-perfect female survival vs. women/first-class advantage vs. a 7.1× ratio).

All three are the same sorted horizontal bar chart with n-counts in the labels, value labels and a Western Europe vs Africa (+2.6) subtitle. The only real differences are that attempt 2 also highlights Africa and the subtitle wording varies slightly.

All three use bar charts in Thursday-to-Sunday order with n under each label. Attempt 1 colours Friday red and its subtitle says 'Friday tips the most', with no CI whiskers or reference line. Attempts 2 and 3 colour every bar the same and add 95% CI whiskers plus an 'All days 16.1%' dashed line, with near-identical 'barely move' subtitles. They differ only in value-label placement (inside the bar vs above it) and colour.

All three show daily bars with a 30-day rolling mean line, a subtitle saying rain falls on 43% of days, and the same wettest-day callout; the only differences are cosmetic: legend versus direct label, how the dates are formatted and slightly different subtitle wording.

All three are row-normalized heatmaps with counts and percentages in each cell, a two-line subtitle on accuracy, class_2's weak recall and the class_2→class_0 error, and no callouts; the only real differences are attempt 3's reversed colormap and small wording and title-case changes.

All three are dumbbell charts sorted by 2020 spending, with the same value labels and growth-multiple callouts and subtitles that make overlapping points; attempt 1 uses a linear axis while attempts 2 and 3 use a log axis, and attempt 3 uses circles instead of diamonds.

All three are blue/red ECDFs with median dots and a threshold callout. Attempts 1 and 2 share a legend, the full x-range and a ≤2 mi callout, while attempt 3 labels the lines directly, cuts the x-axis at 20 mi and uses a >5 mi threshold with its own median callouts.

All three are the same three-line chart with direct end labels and start values; the subtitle wording changes a little between them, and attempt 2's callout is about the largest one-year gain rather than renewables overtaking nuclear.

All three are overlapping ridgelines colored by median with median ticks and a right-hand median column, differing only cosmetically (attempt 2 uses a blue-to-red palette with dashed white ticks); the subtitles all say the medians rise about 18°C and the spread widens, but attempts 1 and 3 add callouts about different things (summer spread vs. July's 80% range) and attempt 2 has no callout.

All three are slope charts sharing the 'every continent gained; Asia most' takeaway with year/value labels at the ends. Attempt 1 highlights only Asia and Africa against gray context lines, adds an Asia–Africa gap line, and has no footnote. Attempts 2 and 3 are nearly identical to each other: every continent gets its own color, marker and line style, and both carry a methodology footnote. Attempt 3 adds vertical axis lines and a one-line subtitle about Africa's gap to the leader, where attempt 2's subtitle says the gap narrowed.

All three are the same line chart with direct labels and a callout at the epoch-37 minimum, but attempt 2 has no shaded overfitting region and its callout adds validation accuracy, while attempt 3 makes validation solid and training dashed and adds end values to the labels.

All three are the same horizontal bar chart with the first-class bar highlighted and the same 2.6x subtitle; they differ only in where the n counts go (after the value, in the axis labels, or in parentheses) and in title capitalization.

All three make the same claim: a subtitle saying 8-cylinder cars have 2.0x the horsepower of 4-cylinder cars, with value labels and n counts on the bars and the 8-cylinder bar highlighted; only the title wording, the axis label and whether the subtitle includes the hp numbers differ.

All three use the same red/blue diverging bars, a dark centred 10-year mean line, a top-left legend and a 2024 record callout. Attempts 1 and 3 both have a subtitle saying every year since 1977 is above zero and add a 1976 last-below-zero callout. Attempt 2 instead uses a takeaway title about the 1.8 °C rise from the 1909 low and calls out the coldest year and the 1973 crossing of the rolling mean.
All three are the same horizontal violin plot with jittered points, red median ticks, the same median labels and n-counts; only the subtitle wording and the jitter positions differ slightly.

All three use the same dumbbell layout, ordering and value labels; attempt 2 marks the average with a diamond and adds a spread column, attempt 3 starts the x-axis near 10, and the subtitles differ (1 and 2 say pretraining raised the floor, 3 names ERNIE as best and BiLSTM as most varied).

All three use the same dot-grid confidence regions, boundary lines, circled misclassified points, colors and legends; the subtitles differ a little: 1 and 2 describe the alcohol and malic-acid splits plus the misplaced count, while 3 gives only the 34/178 (19%) count, and the class labels change (Cultivar 1–3 vs Class 0–2, with n= counts in 3).

All three use the same lower-triangle RdBu heatmap with identical layout and colorbar. All subtitles lead with MPG vs weight (r = -0.83), and attempt2 also notes that displacement and weight move together (r = 0.93); none has in-plot callouts.

All three use the same 2x2 small-multiple layout, with grey lines for individual chicks, a dark mean line with markers, and the end value labelled at the right. Only the wording differs: attempt 1 adds a second subtitle line explaining the lines, attempt 3 says 1.5x instead of +93 g and adds survivor counts, and attempts 2 and 3 put 'mean' in the end labels.

All three use the same two-panel PR/ROC layout with gray fold curves, a navy average line, an orange no-skill baseline and matching footer AUC ranges; they differ only in title wording, attempt 2's added subtitle, and the PR callout (attempt 1 notes the gain over the base rate, while attempts 2 and 3 mark peak precision at different positions).

All three are the same log-scale scatter with continent markers and Qatar and Swaziland callouts. Attempts 2 and 3 are nearly identical, with an upper-left legend that lists medians and slightly reworded labels. Attempt 1 adds a Japan callout, gives r=0.80 in its subtitle and puts a plain legend in the lower right.

All three are the same multi-line chart with the same colors, line styles and end labels. The subtitles differ in which numbers they pick out. Attempts 1 and 3 share the GOOG peak and drop callouts, while attempt 2 instead marks the GOOG listing and the AAPL low.

All three are histograms with a dashed median line at $9.50 and a callout on the $52 JFK flat-fare spike; attempt 1 uses $1 bins and mentions the spike in its subtitle, attempts 1 and 2 color the spike bar red while attempt 3 does not, and the subtitles differ slightly in wording (76% at $15 or less vs 74% under $15).

All three use the same grouped bar chart with red solid female and blue hatched male bars, direct percentage labels and a top-right legend, but the takeaways differ: attempt 1 has a 'widest gap' callout, attempt 2 compares 3rd-class women with 1st-class men, and attempt 3 labels the gap in each class.

All three are sorted horizontal bar charts with the same Western Europe vs Africa subtitle, but attempt 3 highlights Western Europe and Africa (not North America), moves the n counts from the category labels to the end of each bar, and differs slightly in subtitle wording and threshold (n≥5 in attempt 2 vs 10+ in attempts 1 and 3).

All three are the same single-color vertical bar chart in calendar order, with bold value labels, n= counts under each day, and a subtitle giving the 1.7-point spread between Saturday and Friday; only the wording differs slightly, and attempt 3 uses abbreviated day names.

All three are daily bar/spike charts that call out the 55.9 mm wettest day and open with a 43% rainy-days subtitle; attempts 1 and 3 add a 30-day mean overlay with a legend (teal and navy, then grey and red), while attempt 2 shows only the bars and its subtitle names the wettest month instead of the seasonal pattern.

All three use the same rocket heatmap with counts and colorbar and no callouts; the subtitles all lead with 81.5% accuracy, but attempts 1 and 2 name the most common error (class_2 predicted as class_0) while attempt 3 points to class_2's 73% recall instead.

All three are the same dumbbell chart with the same order, colors and legend, and the subtitles say almost the same thing (attempt 3 compares the USA with Japan instead of with the peer average); attempts 1 and 2 use a log scale with the growth multiple between the dots and differ only in where the labels sit, while attempt 3 uses a linear scale and puts the multiple next to the 2020 value.

All three are two-line ECDFs that mark the medians at the 50% line. The subtitles each use a different statistic (share under 3 mi, 21% shorter, median plus 90th percentile), and the median callouts are split in attempts 1 and 3 but combined in attempt 2. On design, attempt 3 cuts the x-axis at 20 mi, uses a legend and adds a note about the trimmed trips, where 1 and 2 label the lines directly. The dashed line is credit card in attempts 2 and 3 but cash in attempt 1.

All three use nearly the same subtitle (renewables 4%→39%, fossil 87%→52%) and end labels, but each adds a different callout: attempt 1 marks the biggest one-year jump in 2009, attempt 2 has no callout, and attempt 3 marks 2009 as the year renewables overtook nuclear and adds start-value labels. On design, attempt 1 is a line chart with highlighted colors and a dashed line for nuclear, while attempts 2 and 3 are matching 100% stacked area charts.

All three use violin plots with jittered dots and red median marks; attempt1 is vertical with an arrow callout on Jun's spread, while attempts 2 and 3 are nearly identical horizontal versions that differ mainly in their subtitles (attempt2 names Jun as most variable and Nov as steadiest; attempt3 explains that each dot is one day).

All three are colour-matched slope charts with direct labels on both ends. Attempt 2 adds arrow callouts for Asia and Oceania and moves the gains out of the labels. Attempt 3 drops the y-axis and gridlines, puts the axis description at the bottom, uses dashed lines for Asia and Africa and leaves out the n counts.

All three are the same line chart: a solid blue training curve, a dashed red validation curve, labels at the line ends and a dot marking the minimum at epoch 37. Attempt 2 adds a vertical line at epoch 37 and a separate '12x' gap callout, and attempt 3 states the gap as 0.095 in its subtitle and uses a vertical arrow above the dot.

All three are the same horizontal bar chart with the first-class bar highlighted, n-counts in the labels and the same 2.6x subtitle; they differ only in subtitle wording, label precision (63% vs 63.0%) and x-axis extent.
All three use the same bar chart, ordering, labels and subtitle, with only one word changed between them; attempt 3 differs by highlighting the 8-cylinder bar in a different color.

All three are the same red/blue diverging bar chart with a dark 10-year rolling mean line and the same record and coldest callouts; only the subtitle takeaways differ, plus small things like gridlines in attempt 2 and x-axis padding.

All three use the same horizontal violin-plus-jitter layout, the same red median ticks, the same median labels and the same n= labels. Only the subtitle wording and the random jitter differ slightly, and two of the subtitles carry the same Gentoo-vs-Adelie and Adelie-Chinstrap message.

All three are the same dumbbell chart, sorted by average, with the same colors and the same min/max/average value labels; they differ only in small title and subtitle wording, such as two of them noting that ERNIE varies least (22.6).

All three plots have the same decision-boundary grid, circled misclassified points, the same two legends and the same '34 of 178' subtitle; only the title wording, label casing and where the subtitle sits differ (it is inside the plot in attempt 1).

All three are the same lower-triangle RdBu heatmap with the same layout, and they share the subtitle 'mpg is most strongly related to weight (r = -0.83)'; only the title wording changes, plus the subtitle's closing clause in attempt 2.

All three use the same 2x2 small-multiples layout, with grey lines for individual chicks, a bold navy mean line, and a nearly identical subtitle; the only real difference is where the day-21 mean callout sits (top-left text box, above the line end, or to the right of the endpoint).

All three use the same two-panel PR/ROC layout with gray fold curves, a dark average line, an orange no-skill baseline and the same AUC-range footnotes; the only differences are the PR legend sitting lower-left in attempt 2 and the title leaving out '(positive = survived)' in attempt 3.

All three are the same log-scale scatter with continents shown by colour and marker and the same three callouts (Japan, Qatar, Swaziland). Only the label wording and the subtitle's takeaway differ: attempts 1 and 3 say Africa lags, while attempt 2 says gains flatten above about $10k.

All three share the same palette, line styles and direct end labels. Attempt 1 uses a linear y-axis with a GOOG-entry callout, while attempts 2 and 3 use a log axis. Their subtitles differ: attempt 1 gives a GOOG/AAPL takeaway, attempt 2 gives growth multiples and adds an MSFT callout and end values, and attempt 3 only explains the log scale.

All three use the same single-color 2-dollar histogram with a dashed median line. The subtitles and callouts differ a little: attempt 1 marks the $52 spike with the median only, attempt 2 adds a mean line and a long-tail callout, and attempt 3 adds a mean line and a flat-fare callout at $52.

All three use the same grouped red/blue bar chart with value labels and legend, differing only in hatching (1 and 3), the n-label format, and subtitle takeaways (overall rates, gap range plus coin flip, third-class women vs first-class men); only attempt 1 adds gap callouts.
